name: Slate-Purple
lede: Slate-Purple is a grayish purple first dated by Ridgway in 1912, the rarest of the library's three slate colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: The rarest of the three
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 standard places this hue on plate XLIV, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classes it as a dark grayish purple, block 229 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[old-lavender]], [[dull-indian-purple]], [[livid-violet]] and [[purplish-grey]], at 3.5, 3.7, 5, 3.7, 4.1 and 4.5 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Slate-Purple in just 33 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.1 percent, as photographed, too rare for any painter or color pairing to stand out reliably [2]. The earliest dated match is a 1491 Chinese handscroll, Shen Zhou's *Twelve Views of Tiger Hill*, four centuries before Ridgway's plate, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that the name existed that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
